raw.query: WITH current_runs AS (SELECT DISTINCT forecast_model AS model FROM provenance.v_dim WHERE is_current = true AND experiment = 'predictors'), p AS (SELECT model, mode, resolution, variate, wape AS pw FROM provenance.forecast_metrics JOIN current_runs USING(model) WHERE span = 'common' AND h = -1 AND candidate = 'point'), q AS (SELECT model, mode, resolution, variate, MIN(wape) AS qw FROM provenance.forecast_metrics WHERE span = 'common' AND h = -1 AND candidate <> 'point' GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4), beaten_stats AS (SELECT p.model, COUNT(*) AS total_cells, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE qw < pw) AS beaten_cells FROM p JOIN q USING(model, mode, resolution, variate) GROUP BY p.model) SELECT model, total_cells, beaten_cells, ROUND((100.0 * beaten_cells / total_cells)::numeric, 1) AS beaten_pct FROM beaten_stats ORDER BY beaten_cells DESC;
raw.observed: TimesFM point forecast is beaten by a quantile in 18/20 cells (90.0% of cells; 17 by p50, 1 by p10). The remaining beaten cells across other models total 33, of which Gaussian-band baselines account for 31 cells (93.9% of the rest).
raw.claimed: TimesFM's mean head is beaten in nearly all its cells by the median or a lower quantile, and the Gaussian-band baselines account for most of the rest
raw.evidence: TimesFM is beaten in 18/20 cells (all by p50 or p10), and 31 of the remaining 33 beaten cells are accounted for by classical baselines (Holt-Winters 16, EWMA 9, Naive 6).
